headline: 195 Lake View went from nine days of silence to a live negotiation in one morning — a new offer landed at 8:13, you countered $355K, and the only thing still blocking it is your own ruling on the co-op's 3.5% commission ask · DO: rule the 3.5% and send the counter · WATCH: an unverified listing inquiry sent a lookalike meeting link — do not open it.

notes: 🔴 ONE BLOCKED LINE IN THE WINDOW AND IT IS THE SAME DEPENDENCY THAT HAS FAILED TWICE TODAY: the 12:22 Brivity deep sweep went BLOCKED because chrome.exe was not running — Parts A/B/C/E blind. It fell back to the API-only path and did the honest thing (queue empty, zero outbound), so nothing was sent wrong; the cost is that the CRM-side verification lane is dark this afternoon. The 5:17 AM marketing run hit a DIFFERENT Chrome failure — "multiple browsers connected, none selected" — so the browser layer has now produced two distinct faults in one day. Everything else since yesterday ran clean.

✅ THE MORNING BLOCK LIST EMPTIED ITSELF BY LUNCH, AND IT WAS THE COMMAND CHANNEL THAT DID IT. The 9:52 Delta executed FIFTEEN of your commands, thirteen of them through the Todoist comment channel on its first day of real volume — none of which any routine had acknowledged before. Three things this board has been carrying as open decisions are now RULED and closed: the 9:00 double-book, the reconnect-lane cap question (keep both lanes, cap restored, ruling written into the database routine's read path so it stops re-cutting itself), and the frozen teammate-ownership call.

⚠️ AND THAT FROZEN INQUIRY CLOSED THE WRONG WAY, WHICH IS STILL USEFUL: your teammate answered at 10:22 that the Compass inquiry she was handed is a scam, and that she has been getting a lot of them. That verdict points straight at a second inquiry on a live listing with the identical shape — recorded as a pattern match, not a verdict, because one teammate's read on a different lead is a single source.

callBlock.who: Unverified 2127 Hwy 93 inquiry — she sent a replacement meeting link at 10:09 and it is not Google's
callBlock.why: 🛑 THE TELL FIRED, AND THE WARNING THAT PREDICTED IT HAD ALREADY BEEN CHECKED OFF TWO HOURS EARLIER. The control said, verbatim, do not click a replacement link if one arrives. At 10:06 you asked whether she was getting on the call; at 10:08 she said YOUR link was broken in every browser she tried; at 10:09 she sent her own room instead. The registrable domain on that link is a Spanish-registry lookalike and the Google part is a path segment, not the hostname — that is verifiable from the text of the URL alone, without opening anything, and nothing opened it. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED: what is behind it. You do not need to know in order to not click it. ✅ YOUR INSTINCT WAS ALREADY RIGHT — you drafted a reply re-sending your own real link at 10:12, and that draft is still sitting unsent. Send that; do not take hers, on any device. ⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS SHARPER TODAY THAN YESTERDAY: your teammate independently called a structurally identical inquiry on another listing a scam at 10:22 this morning — same template opener, same phone refusal, same overseas alibi, same push to video with a third party added. Two of the same shape on two listings in six days. ⛔ THE LINE THAT DOES NOT MOVE: still no proof of fraud and she may yet be real, but nothing sensitive until identity is established — no seller information, no showing access, no lockbox codes, no title or wiring detail. She still has no phone number anywhere, which remains the cleanest test.

callBlock.who: Donna M. — a brand-new lead on your own Fieldstone listing whose email bounced on arrival
callBlock.why: 🔥 INBOUND AT 9:23 THIS MORNING ON YOUR OWN INVENTORY, AND THE AUTOMATED LANE WAS DEAD FOUR MINUTES LATER. The instant responder emailed her at 9:27:35 and the message hard-bounced at 9:27:38 — address not found. There is no second automated channel. The phone is the entire play and the machine has already used its only shot. ⚠️ The address on file looks like a typo of her own name; a corrected spelling is an obvious guess and the machine will not guess it or email a made-up address. If she gives you the right one on the call it goes in the CRM and the email lane reopens. ⭐ SHE IS WARMER THAN AN AD CLICK: two notifications fired in the same minute — the ad alert and a registration on your own site — so she both clicked the ad and signed up. She raised her hand on the $380K Helena listing, which is the one that just took the first showing it has ever had, an hour and a half ago. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED: her timeline, whether she is relocating, whether she is working with anyone, or whether the phone number is any more accurate than the email was. If the number is dead too, this lead has no channel at all — and that is worth knowing today rather than next week. Ownership is verified off the webhook payload, not inferred.

callBlock.who: Cheryl G. — she asked for a Mt Laurel search last night and the promise is still open
callBlock.why: 🔥 SHE REPLIED, AND THE GOODBYE EMAIL IS WHAT DID IT. After three touches and five days of silence, the soft close-out went out yesterday morning and she answered ten and a half hours later, asking about a specific house. That is the single most useful script result the cadence engine has produced this month. ⭐ THE OWED THING IS INVENTORY, NOT A CALL BACK: the house she asked about is under contract, you told her so, and she came back with the real brief — Mt Laurel, not much above $600K. You then asked her must-haves and that question has been sitting unanswered about eighteen hours now. Pull active and coming-soon in and around Mt Laurel in her band and send it, sourced truthfully — never invent a listing to fill the promise. ⚠️ Worth knowing before you dial: 89 visits and 172 views at an average viewed price near $552K, so $600K sits right on top of her actual behavior. She is also potentially TWO-SIDED — you have exchanged mail about her own address twice this spring, and a Mt Laurel purchase probably needs that house sold. Nobody has ever asked her that.

Your own task, due mid-December: send card, husband's health not good. Behind it, in your own notes: they own two Orange Beach condos plus a Foley house, and they told you they want to sell two of them. A Hoover household holding three Gulf Coast properties with two stated seller intents, in the market you are actively building — attached to a promise you made and did not keep. ⚠️ THE CARD COMES FIRST AND THE MACHINE TOOK ZERO TOUCHES HERE ON PURPOSE. The health note is seven months old; if it resolved badly, a listing conversation opened cold is the wrong move. Not asserted: his health, whether either property already sold, or whether they still want to sell. All three are the call, and none of them are the card. This name sat inside two summary tasks that both got checked off while the underlying item stayed overdue.

callBlock.who: Keith T. — "wants to discuss selling," and nobody has ever emailed him
callBlock.why: 📞 THE BEST UN-WORKED AT-BAT ON A 73-DEEP OVERDUE BOARD, AND THE TASK TEXT IS YOURS, NOT MACHINE NOISE: "Call!! Wants to discuss selling see notes" — due the first of December, roughly eight months overdue. ⭐ A 400-day mail check across both your addresses found ZERO emails to him, ever. The only activity on the record is your own note from late November saying a mailer went out. And the CRM scores his property a low sell score, so this is an at-bat, not a layup. It is a free at-bat on a record that has never once been worked, and anything he told you in November may already have happened. He is callable — no DNC flag. The "see notes" points at a note that only says "sent mailer"; the real context lives in your memory, not the CRM.

callBlock.who: Chris C. — the reconnect email is now unblocked, but the call is still the better version
callBlock.why: ⏰ THE 9:15 HOLD RESOLVED ITSELF THIS MORNING AND IT RESOLVED YOUR WAY. He was row 3 of 5 on today's relationship-reconnect batch and the ISA flagged him HOLD before the batch fired; the other four rows went clean. 🔴 WHY HE WAS HELD: the last thing on his record is HIS message to you asking for his closing paperwork disc and his warranty — and it was never answered. Eighteen months of silence since. A no-agenda check-in offering to run his equity number is the wrong first sentence to a man whose last request went unanswered. ⭐ THE CALL IS THE BETTER INSTRUMENT ANYWAY: two minutes to find out whether he ever got the disc and the warranty, and then the equity conversation is welcome instead of tone-deaf. Past client, closed with you, and his wife has already told you you're awesome. ⚠️ Not asserted: whether this was quietly resolved off-email at the time. If it was, this is a thirty-second feel-good call instead of a repair call. ⭐ It also exposed a real staging bug worth knowing: the batch classified him as having no interaction ever logged, which is true in the CRM and false in reality — there are ten-plus mail threads on him including the complaint. Any relationship that lived in email reads as untouched to that lane.

callBlock.who: John D. — your own task says send him numbers, and his phone is DNC-flagged
callBlock.why: ⚖️ THIS IS A DECISION CHIP, NOT A DIAL ORDER — READ THE DNC LINE FIRST. Your task, due the third of July and about four weeks overdue, reads: send numbers and detail, nail it, six-month listing potential. ⚠️ There are no notes on his record — the panel is empty, same shape as the other overdue seller on this list. Whatever "see notes" points at lives in your memory, not the CRM. ⭐ HE IS NOT UN-WORKED, WHICH CHANGES THE PLAY: two ISA emails went out this month, on the 23rd and the 27th, plus three older ones. Zero replies. So the missing piece is not another check-in — it is the NUMBERS your own task asked for: a real market read on his address, not a generic touch. 🔴 THE DNC QUESTION IS YOURS, NOT THE MACHINE'S: he submitted his own number through your home-value form, which is a different situation than a cold purchased row, but the ISA will not overrule a DNC flag on its own. If the flag applies, the play is a numbers email or a mailer and nothing else. ⚠️ Not asserted: whether he still owns the property, or whether six-month listing potential is still live eight months later. His record is also flagged a duplicate and worth a merge look.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $369K — a NEW offer landed 8:13 this morning and your $355K counter is waiting on one ruling
listings.note: 🔥 NINE DAYS OF SILENCE ENDED IN ONE MORNING AND THIS IS NOW THE MOST LIVE FILE ON THE BOARD. The buyer's agent shared three documents at 8:13:12 with the line that matters: his sellers go under contract on THEIR house this morning. The action did not change: rule the commission number, because her delivering the sheet does not establish how she treated the 3.5% ask. ⛔ DO NOT QUOTE $355,000 AS THE OFFER — it is YOUR COUNTER. The actual offer price, terms and expiry are still unverified: they live inside dotloop documents no routine has opened, and none will guess at them. ⚠️ Two older items still open: the 7/19 showing has been re-asked six times with nothing back, and at six asks the silence IS the feedback; and Sunday's cancelled 3:00 showing still has not been rebooked at six days — the buyer got called into work, which is a reschedule, not a lost buyer.
